sections.html: Labeo cyclorhynchus becomes about 16 cm long. The name "variegatus" is regarded nowadays only as a synonym of Labeo cyclorhynchus. The checkered variety occurs in the wild but bears no scientific name of its own.
This species of Labeo is imported from the Congo.
Like all Labeos these fish are quarrelsome against conspecifics, but L. cyclorhynchus in particular is regarded as quite peaceful against other species of fish.

Usually this species has long, sickle-shaped dorsal fins. But one of the specimens has a "normal"-shaped dorsal fin. This possibly is a sexual dimorphism. Possibly the "Variegatus" morph is most often linked to male specimens? So far nobody knows.
The checkered variety is maybe best compared with the so-called OB-morphs in Mbuna cichlids from Lake Malawi. The "normal" variety of Labeo cyclorhynchus is hardly ever imported.
